newsitem.title: USA: Coca-Cola Enterprises sees profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola Enterprises sees profit growth.

text.p: Coca-Cola Enterprises Inc Tuesday reported 21 percent growth in the first quarter in cash operating profit and said it is on track to produce nine percent comparable cash operating profit growth and 10 to 15 percent earnings per share growth in 1997.
It said first quarter cash operating profit reached $274 million, reflecting 21 percent reported growth and eight percent comparable growth.
Excluding a one percent dilution from currency translations, the first-quarter 1997 growth in comparable cash operating profit was nine percent, it said.

Comparable first-quarter performance adjusts reported results to exclude a favorable supplier settlement and to include the same acquisitions for the same periods that are reflected in the first quarter 1997, the company said.
It said first-quarter consolidated constant territory volume increased 10 percent, with physical cases in the company's territories growing nine percent in the United States and 14 percent in Europe.
Due to previously announced noncash stock compensation expenses, the company said, the first-quarter net loss per share was $0.27.
The loss includes a $0.03 per share one-time charge for the redemption of certain debentures.

"We are pleased with the strength of our first-quarter 1997 performance, particularly considering the highly competitive pricing environment that we are seeing in the United States," said Chief Executive Summerfield Johnston Jr.
"The company is on track to produce nine percent comparable cash operating profit growth and 10 percent to 15 percent earnings per share growth in 1997.

"With our continued investment in people and infrastructure in the United States and Europe, we are confident in our ability to generate consistent growth in financial and operating results that will increase long-term share-owner value."

The company said its adjusted first-quarter 1997 net loss of $0.24 per share includes the previously announced increase in noncash selling, general, and administrative expenses relating to certain stock compensation plans and the dilutive effect of its new European operations.

European consumption patterns are significantly more seasonal than in the United States, it said. As a result, first-quarter and fourth-quarter European volume does not typically generate operating results that fully offset fixed costs such as depreciation, amortization and interest expense, Coca-Cola Enterprises said.
